headline: Inside Cameroon's Prison Studio: Where Inmates Find Freedom Through Music
meta_description: New Bell prison in Douala, Cameroon, hosts Jail Time Records—a studio and label giving inmates a creative outlet. A documentary just won at Tribeca.
summary_short: A music studio inside New Bell prison in Cameroon is transforming inmates' lives through art. The documentary about it won three awards at Tribeca.
body:
Deep inside New Bell, a notorious prison in Douala, Cameroon, a small recording booth and a solitary computer have become instruments of profound change. Jail Time Records—a music studio and label founded in 2018—has given voice to some of the facility's most talented inmates, producing songs that have reached listeners across South Africa, the US, and Argentina. One prisoner-artist named Empereur accumulated 24,000 YouTube views with a music video filmed entirely within the prison walls. This year, the studio's impact was recognized globally when a documentary about Jail Time Records, directed by co-founders Steve Happi and Italian artist Dione Roach, won three prizes at New York's Tribeca film festival, including best documentary feature. "It's this instrument of resistance where we can really share friendship, love and our voices can be heard," Happi, a former inmate himself, tells the BBC. "We don't think anymore about the four walls—we find the freedom."

New Bell houses roughly 4,700 prisoners—four times its intended capacity—within crumbling walls marked by violence, unsanitary conditions, and desperation. Yet within this brutal environment, music has become a lifeline. The studio's rudimentary setup belies its output: high-production music videos featuring complex storytelling and dozens of fellow inmates as actors and crew. When Roach first heard rappers freestyling during a dance class in 2018, she approached prison authorities for permission to build a studio. They agreed, recognizing music's power in their deeply musical nation.

The project extends beyond entertainment. In 2022, Happi and Roach released an album, Jail Time Vol 1, with profits split equally between artists and reinvestment in the label. The studio has also expanded to include women prisoners, with artist Jeje making her debut in 2022. Oscar-winning director Taika Waititi, who served as executive producer for the documentary, describes the music emerging from New Bell as "amazing," calling creative outlets "an incredibly powerful and humane thing" for those serving long sentences.
quick_facts: New Bell prison in Douala, Cameroon holds 4,700 inmates at four times capacity
Jail Time Records studio founded 2018, won three awards at Tribeca 2024
Prisoner Empereur's music video reached 24,000 YouTube views from inside prison
Documentary directed by Steve Happi and Dione Roach, filmed over six years
